name: Texas Instruments Incorporated
executive_summary: Texas Instruments is a high-quality analog and embedded-processing franchise recovering from the 2024 semiconductor down-cycle, with primary filings showing revenue re-acceleration, margin expansion and a step-change in free cash flow as capital expenditure normalises. The quantitative screen rates TXN a buy on growth-adjusted value (PEG 0.94, PEGY 0.19), quality, dividend and financial health, despite a headline P/E of 48.8 that reflects trough-to-recovery earnings rather than peak-cycle normalisation. The central debate is whether trailing-twelve-month FCF of $6.5 billion (33.6% of revenue per the Q2 2026 10-Q) justifies accumulation at current multiples, or whether the pending ~$7.5 billion Silicon Labs acquisition and cyclical exposure cap upside. Deep research broadly confirms the screen’s quality and cash-generation case, but flags integration, leverage and valuation timing as reasons for measured rather than aggressive sizing.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, TXN offers a rare combination of structural moat, shareholder-return discipline and cyclical recovery at a point where earnings and cash flow are inflecting upward. Management’s stated North Star—free cash flow per share—aligns with the screen’s dividend-growth, economic-moat, Piotroski F-score and financial-health passes. The business model is deliberately differentiated: owned 300mm manufacturing, broad analog catalogue, long product lifecycles and end-market exposure weighted to industrial, automotive and data centre—all cited repeatedly in SEC filings as sustainable competitive advantages.

The screen’s buy signal is not driven by absolute cheapness (P/B 15.2, P/E 48.8) but by growth-adjusted metrics: reported growth of 51.8% and PEG/PEGY well below 1.0 suggest the market still prices TXN on depressed 2024 earnings ($5.20 diluted EPS per FY2024 10-K) rather than the recovery evident in H1 2026 ($3.82 diluted EPS in six months per Q2 2026 10-Q). ROE of 35.2% and a ~2.0% yield, with dividends rising ($5.50/share in 2025 per FY2025 10-K), reinforce the quality-and-income pillar. CHIPS Act incentives (35% ITC, up to $1.6 billion direct funding) structurally lower the cost base and are already flowing through cash taxes and capex offsets—supporting the screen’s GARP and risk-model passes. For value investors willing to underwrite a cyclical upturn and tolerate a rich headline multiple, TXN fits the screen’s accumulate profile: franchise quality is high, cash conversion is improving sharply, and capital return remains a management priority.
financial_review:
*Primary source: SEC filing body extracts unless noted.*

**Annual trend (10-K)**

| Metric | FY2023 (10-K FY2024) | FY2024 (10-K FY2024) | FY2025 (10-K filed Feb 2026) |
|--------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------------------|
| Revenue | $17.519bn | $15.641bn (−10.7%) | $17.682bn (+13.0%) |
| Net income | $6.510bn | $4.799bn | $5.001bn |
| Diluted EPS | $7.07 | $5.20 | $5.45 |
| Operating profit / margin | $7.331bn / 41.8% | $5.465bn / 34.9% | $6.023bn / 34.1% |
| Gross margin | 62.9% | 58.1% | 57.0% |
| Cash from operations | $6.420bn | $6.318bn | $7.153bn |
| Free cash flow | $1.349bn (7.7% of rev.) | $1.498bn (9.6%) | $2.938bn (16.6%) |
| Capital expenditure | $5.071bn | $4.820bn | $4.550bn |
| Total debt (carrying) | — | $13.60bn | $14.05bn |
| Dividends paid | $4.557bn | $4.795bn | $4.999bn |

FY2024 was the trough of the analog/embedded down-cycle: revenue fell across Analog (−7%) and Embedded Processing (−25%), with gross margin compressing on lower factory loadings and elevated capex for 300mm fab build-out. FY2025 marked recovery—Analog revenue +15% to $14.0bn, total revenue +13%—but gross margin dipped further to 57.0% as capacity-expansion depreciation and LFAB ramp costs weighed on Embedded Processing (operating margin 11.3% vs 37.9% for Analog). Restructuring charges of $117m in 2025 included planned closure of two remaining 150mm fabs and a goodwill impairment on custom ASIC products (FY2025 10-K). No going-concern language appears in available filing extracts; liquidity is described as adequate for at least 12 months.

**Interim trend (10-Q)**

The recovery has accelerated into 2026:

- **Q2 2026** (10-Q filed 24 Jul 2026): Revenue $5.46bn (+23% YoY); net income $1.98bn; diluted EPS $2.14; gross margin 61.4% (up from 57.9%); operating margin 42.3%. Broad growth in industrial, data centre and automotive.
- **H1 2026**: Revenue $10.29bn (+21%); net income $3.53bn; diluted EPS $3.82; gross margin 59.8%; operating margin 40.0%.
- **Trailing twelve months to Jun 2026**: Revenue $19.45bn; cash from operations $8.67bn; free cash flow **$6.53bn** (33.6% of revenue)—a 271% increase vs the prior TTM. Capex TTM fell to $3.31bn; CHIPS Act proceeds TTM $1.18bn.
- **Balance sheet (Jun 2026)**: Cash plus investments $7.0bn (up $2.1bn from Dec 2025); inventory $4.61bn with days falling to 196 from 222 at year-end 2025.

FY2025 10-K guides capex to **$2–3bn in 2026**, down from the elevated $4.5bn cycle—consistent with the interim run-rate ($1.19bn in H1 2026). A $5bn delayed-draw term loan facility was arranged in Jun 2026 to fund the pending Silicon Labs acquisition; no borrowings drawn as of quarter-end.

**Gaps:** Nine of nineteen indexed 8-K filings lack body extracts; risk-factor detail in interim filings incorporates by reference to the FY2025 10-K rather than restating full Item 1A text in the corpus. Yahoo `financials_annual.json` aligns with filing figures for FY2023–FY2025 and was not required for core P&L; quarterly Yahoo data shows Q2 2026 revenue $4.825bn vs $5.46bn in the 10-Q—filings take precedence and that discrepancy is not reconciled here.
risks_and_flags:
**Cyclical and operational.** Filings describe semiconductor cycles explicitly: demand swings drive revenue, and fixed manufacturing costs amplify margin volatility when factory loadings fall. The FY2024 trough demonstrated this sharply; any renewed inventory correction or macro slowdown could reverse the current margin expansion.

**Capex and capacity.** Net PPE reached $12.3bn at Dec 2025 (FY2025 10-K). While capex is declining, underutilisation during downturns remains a structural risk. LFAB ramp continues to weigh on Embedded Processing economics until fully loaded.

**Acquisition and leverage.** The definitive agreement to acquire Silicon Labs for ~$7.5bn enterprise value (cash, expected H1 2027 close) will be funded from cash and debt—including a $5bn delayed-draw facility. Integration, regulatory approval and return-on-capital scrutiny are unresolved. Transaction-related charges of $34m YTD in 2026 are already flowing through Other segment results.

**Customer and geographic concentration.** One end customer accounted for 12% of revenue in both 2024 and 2025 (Analog-weighted). China represented 21% of revenue in 2025; trade-policy and geopolitical risks are flagged in forward-looking statements.

**Restructuring and impairments.** FY2025 restructuring ($117m) and custom ASIC goodwill impairment signal portfolio rationalisation; further charges possible as 150mm fab closures proceed.

**Regulatory and incentives.** CHIPS Act direct-funding agreements contain “representations, warranties and covenants” with “events of default and related rights and remedies, including clawbacks” (FY2025 10-K, Note 2). OBBBA tax changes raised the 2025 effective rate to 12.4%; future rate benefits are uncertain.

**Pension.** Underfunded retirement plans of $124m at Dec 2025; net periodic benefit costs are modest ($30m U.S. defined benefit in 2025) but discount-rate sensitivity remains.

**Governance.** Form 8-K (16 Oct 2025): Executive Chairman Richard Templeton to retire 31 Dec 2025; CEO Haviv Ilan becomes chairman—a planned succession, not a disruption, but a leadership transition nonetheless.

**Debt service.** Interest expense rose to $543m in 2025 (+$35m YoY) on additional issuance; total debt ~$14bn. Fixed-rate structure limits cash-flow volatility from rates, but principal repayment capacity depends on sustained FCF.

**Legal/contingencies.** Commitments and contingencies referenced in Note 10; no material going-concern qualification in available extracts. Uncertain tax positions: $87m liability at Dec 2025.
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is **material and earnings-centric**, not thin—though much is syndicated commentary rather than primary corporate disclosure.

**Earnings (Jul 2026):** “TI reports second quarter 2026 financial results and shareholder returns” (PR Newswire, 22 Jul 2026); “Texas Instruments (NASDAQ:TXN) Reports Bullish Q2, Inventory Levels Improve” (Yahoo Finance, 22 Jul 2026). TXN beat Q2 estimates and raised outlook, yet shares fell—widely reported (“Texas Instruments Delivers Beat-And-Raise Earnings Report, But Stock Falls Late,” Investor’s Business Daily, 22 Jul 2026; “Texas Instruments tops second-quarter forecasts but shares slip despite strong outlook,” Yahoo Finance, 23 Jul 2026).

**Sector sentiment (Jul 2026):** Broader semi weakness weighed on TXN post-earnings (“Tech Stocks Slide as Semiconductor Index Drops 6% Despite Strong Earnings,” Yahoo Finance, 24 Jul 2026; “Texas Instruments (TXN) Faces Decline Amid Semiconductor Sector Weakness,” GuruFocus, 25 Jul 2026).

**Valuation debate:** Contrasting views—“Texas Instruments Generates Strong Free Cash Flow - But TXN Stock Looks Cheap to Value Buyers” (Yahoo Finance, 24 Jul 2026) vs “Texas Instruments (TXN) Stock Looks Fully Valued After A 75% Run” (simplywall.st, 24 Jul 2026) and “Texas Instruments Inc (TXN) Stock Down 3.1% but Still Overvalued” (GuruFocus, 23 Jul 2026).

**Analyst actions:** Rosenblatt maintained with PT raised to $350 (GuruFocus, 24 Jul 2026); Mizuho PT raised to $305 (GuruFocus, 23 Jul 2026).

**Strategy/M&A:** Silicon Labs acquisition (~$7.5bn) disclosed in FY2025 10-K and Q2 2026 10-Q; no separate press release body in the news manifest beyond earnings coverage.

**Management:** Templeton retirement and Ilan chair appointment (8-K, 16 Oct 2025)—limited follow-on news in the manifest.

**Dividend narrative:** “Texas Instruments vs. Qualcomm: One Pays Out 94% of Earnings…” (Yahoo Finance, 24 Jul 2026)—highlights payout intensity as a talking point.
research_rationale: Primary filings confirm a cyclical recovery with sharply improving free cash flow and balance-sheet optionality, supporting the quantitative buy signal on quality and growth-adjusted value, though headline multiples, Silicon Labs integration risk and sector cyclicality warrant a measured accumulate rather than unqualified conviction.
